ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit diagram shows a p-i-n photodiode connected to the inverting input node of an ideal op-amp. The non-inverting input is grounded. A feedback resistor labeled 1 MΩ connects the op-amp output V0 back to the inverting input node. The op-amp has ±VCC supplies, and the output node is connected to a load resistor labeled 10 kΩ going to ground. There is also a 1 MΩ resistor in the photodiode bias path to +VCC. Reasoning: The light-generated photodiode current is Iph = responsivity × incident optical power = 0.8 A/W × 10 μW = 0.8 × 10 × 10^-6 A = 8 μA. With the 1 MΩ feedback resistor seen in the image, the transimpedance output voltage magnitude is |V0| = Iph Rf = 8 μA × 1 MΩ = 8 V. Since 8 V is within the ±15 V supply rails, the op-amp is not saturated. The load resistor in the image is RL = 10 kΩ, so the load current magnitude is |IL| = |V0| / RL = 8 V / 10 kΩ = 0.0008 A = 800 μA.
